characters.name: Beef Tobin
characters.description: A fisherman and the patriarch of the Tobins. He's still recovering from being divorced by his wife, Kathleen, which results in him doing everything possible to keep his kids close by. Action Dad: Combined withPapa Wolf. In "Tusk in the Wind Adventure," Beef leaps into action without hesitation both times Wolf is in harm’s way, first by cutting Wolf out of the net he’s stuck in that Tusk is trying to put in the water, and second when Wolf gets trapped on a decomposing log over a ravine. Aerith and Bob: Beef's brother is named Brian. Animal Motifs: Beef is often compared to a bear, most likely due to his stocky build, along with his strength and hirsutism. The first instance was inRomantic Meat-Based Adventurewhere his family had to strangle him down to the ground while fighting them off like a wild bear. The second was inBear of Beeftown Adventure, where he compares himself to The Kid, especially with his conflict while dating Carissa. Finally, inA Chugs Life Adventure, he was called "the Dare Bear" when in the past he was quite theparty animalwhen drunk and would take on any dare. Berserk Button: Calls an indoor tree at the mall "an abomination" and takes it with him when he leaves.

characters.name: Judy Tobin
characters.description: The sixteen-year-old and only daughter of the Tobins. She works in the photography studio at the local mall and shows an interest in arts and journalism. Allegedly Dateless: Despite being described as a hopeless romantic, nerdy, awkward and even lamenting about such, Judy has had a significant amount of love interests throughout the show that have returned her affection, most notably in "You've Got Sail Adventure" when she was on a date withthree separate boys at the same time. Ambiguously Bi:In "Beef's Craig Beef Adventure" Judy finds Londra's team of fisherwomen sexy and decides she's going to unpack some of those thoughts later.In "Skidmark Holmes Adventure", she replies to a spam text about meeting "big-boobied singles in your area" with "maybe another time". In "Beef's Craig Beef Adventure" Judy finds Londra's team of fisherwomen sexy and decides she's going to unpack some of those thoughts later. In "Skidmark Holmes Adventure", she replies to a spam text about meeting "big-boobied singles in your area" with "maybe another time".

characters.name: Wolf Tobin
characters.description: The eldest 22-year-old son of the Tobins. He was engaged to Honeybee and marries her in the Season 1 finale. Ambiguously Bi: While he clearly loves Honeybee, he shows open attraction to males; this can range from accidental double entendres to openly calling men attractive (many times referring to his father). This is much less ambiguous after "Beef's in Toyland Adventure", where it's revealed that one of him and Honeybee's pastimes is to rate hot men together and approach them if they're attractive enough.Approach them for what?Wolf and Honeybee don't seem sure themselves.It's framed as a couple who areboth interested in an open relationshipbut haven't quite figured that out consciously. Big Brother Instinct: Is the most vocally upset when Judy plans to quit her job at the mall before she evens starts it, and he tells Beef he and Honeybee are moving partly to get Beef's focus off Judy. Birds of a Feather: Has this dynamic with is wife Honeybee. They're both movie lovers who have similar ambitions and desires regarding their turning passions for film into a business of some kind. Wolf tends to be a bit more immature and prone to flights of fancy than Honeybee, but they also often get caught up in the same types of schemes. Determinator: Cutting both his hands, peeing his pants, hurting his ab muscles, and sobbing from all the pain doesn’t stop Wolf from competing in the Daver Dash.

characters.name: Ham Tobin
characters.description: The gay seventeen-year-old middle son of the Tobins. He takes over as the town's "Cake Lady". The Ditz:He's not the brightest child in the family and quickly forgets things, like that he's already out of the closet.Ham: We should have realized it sooner, but in fairness to me, I never realize things sooner.Season 2 seems to downplay this and make him more of aGenius Ditz. He is shown reading more and is able to catch on when something is amiss, while still having lovably clueless moments. He's not the brightest child in the family and quickly forgets things, like that he's already out of the closet.Ham: We should have realized it sooner, but in fairness to me, I never realize things sooner. Season 2 seems to downplay this and make him more of aGenius Ditz. He is shown reading more and is able to catch on when something is amiss, while still having lovably clueless moments. Embarrassing Middle Name: His middle name is revealed to bePiercebrosnanand Moon reveals Kathleen had some wine during Ham's birth when she came up with that name.

characters.name: Moon Tobin
characters.description: The ten-year-old and youngest son of the Tobins. He's interested in survivalism and searching for cryptids in the woods. All Boys Want Bad Girls: Early on, it was heavily implied that he actually had a repressed crush on Debbie, the meanest girl in his class, or at least a desire for her to see him as "hot". However, this crush was later ditched by Season 3 as Debbie turned into his platonic bully friend whileNice GirlQuinn became his new primaryLove Interest. Animal Lover: Moon is an outdoorsy boy who has successfully befriended many animals, including a falcon, a reindeer, many skunks, wolf pups, moose, full-grown bears, and more. Big Eater: Despite being the youngest and smallest, this growing boy sure has the biggest appetite out of his entire family. This is most notable in the Thanksgiving episode "Good Beef Hunting Adventure" where he beats his siblings at a cranberry sauceEating Contest. The Comically Serious: He's a lot sterner than the rest of his family, made even more hilarious by the fact that he's a little boy.

characters.name: Honeybee Shaw-Tobin
characters.description: Wolf's fiancée, and later wife, who moved from Fresno, California. Audience Surrogate: Because she intends to live with Wolf's family when they get married, she, along with the audience, gets to learn more about the Tobins and the things they do in Alaska. Big Sister Instinct:Befitting her role as Judy's big sister-in-law, Honeybee sounds ready to beat the tar out of someone when she mistakenly thinks Judy got her heart broken in "Pride & Prejudance Adventure".In "Sister Pact Too Adventure", while at a feminist retreat, a retreat staff offers Judy a cup with a liquid inside to drink, but shestops Judy from taking it as they later learn the liquid in the cup is breast milk. After learning that the person in charge of the retreat is running a multi-level marketing scheme and displays behavior of a cult leader, her first instinct is to get Judy away from the retreat. Befitting her role as Judy's big sister-in-law, Honeybee sounds ready to beat the tar out of someone when she mistakenly thinks Judy got her heart broken in "Pride & Prejudance Adventure". In "Sister Pact Too Adventure", while at a feminist retreat, a retreat staff offers Judy a cup with a liquid inside to drink, but shestops Judy from taking it as they later learn the liquid in the cup is breast milk. After learning that the person in charge of the retreat is running a multi-level marketing scheme and displays behavior of a cult leader, her first instinct is to get Judy away from the retreat.

characters.name: Dirtrude "Aunt Dirt" Tobin
characters.description: Beef's long-lost aunt, who has been living in a bunker on the property for 60 years. After the family happens upon her bunker one day, she officially moves in with them and has been a member of the main cast ever since. Artistic License – Gun Safety: Being someone stuck inThe '60s, she uses guns like they're toys and has even aimed at her own family members. Despite this, none of them have ever so much as remarked on her recklessness. Butch Lesbian: Very gruff and masculine, and a confirmed lesbian. Dirty Old Woman: Being 85 years old doesn't deter her from groping any lady she finds attractive. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In her debut episode, "Aunt Misbehavin' Adventure", Aunt Dirt was depicted with grey hair. Starting in "Cheese’s All That Adventure" and onwards, she is now depicted with white hair not long after she first appeared in the series.

characters.name: Kathleen Tobin
characters.description: Beef's ex-wife and the mother of his children who left him for another man. Abusive Parents: While we don't know the full extent of it (other than leaving the Tobin kids home alone all the time and naming the family dog "Grandma" to pretend that an adult was watching them), Judy outright says that Kathleen was a bad mother and that things actually improved after she abandoned the Tobins. In "The Yawn of the Dead Adventure", it's stated that she handed over the newly-born Moon to Judy and Ham and bluntly told them to take care of him. Burner Phones: As a criminal, she would always carry these and her own family can't even get into contact with her once she disposes of them for a new one. Daddy Didn't Show: Judy states she's a flake and she would have missed her birth if it was medically possible. Naturally, despite the other Tobin's fears (and secret hopes) that she would come to Wolf's wedding, she doesn't show. "Dear John" Letter: She left her family a goodbye letter that said "Smell you later" and has a drawing of a middle finger where the fingers are replaced with penises.

characters.name: Brian Tobin
characters.description: Beef's older brother who runs a hot tub business in Anchorage. City Mouse:Played With. Brian was born and raised in Lone Moose, and fit in quite well with the town, being a previous champion in the Danver Dash with Beef. But in comparison to his nature-loving brother, whilst he enjoys participating in wilderness activities and visiting, Brian actually prefers the big city life of living in Anchorage. Cool Uncle: Is regarded highly by all of Beef's children but especially Wolf, who admires how well he performed in the 'Daver Dash. Sibling Rivalry: Can get competitive with his brother at times, especially more so when they were kids like in "Boy Meats World Adventure". Sibling Yin-Yang: Played with. Beef and Brian are similar in personality and get along well, but Brian never took to nature or rustic living the way that Beef did and much prefers living in the city.

characters.name: Becca Tobin
characters.description: Bookworm: Always has her face in a book. Brainy Brunette: She has dark brown hair and is always reading a book. Catchphrase: "Can I finish this page?" Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Has not been seen since Season 1 despite her father regularly appearing. Given that her mother never appeared alongside Brain,it's likely that her parents are divorced and share joint custody over her, thus explaining why she's not always around. Kissing Cousins: Subverted in that while she's Ham's date to the dance, there's no romance between them (or any of her cousins for that matter).

characters.name: Danica Tobin
characters.description: Beef and Brian's cousin who's very uptight and judgmental, and also a bank robber. Graceful Loser: Despite Chief Edna and Elba stopping her and arresting her, she admits defeat without making a fuss out of it, but still insults their appearance. Indubitably Uninteresting Individual: Criminal past and unpleasant personality aside, she's a thoroughly dull person. Her entire house is brown because all other colors are too showy for her. She has a porcelain rabbit collection that consists of one rabbit. Her cellar pantry is full of nothing but (opened) mayonnaise. Jerkass: She never stops insulting or being critical of people. It's this exact behavior that makes Ham seek her out, as he hopes that, given her bad attitude, she'll have a more intense reaction to Ham's coming out than the rest of his family, though Beef worries she'll be too intense and actually hurt Ham's feelings. Ham never did get to tell her. Justified Criminal: Play straight first and then subverted. She reveals she was a bank robber because she got fired from her job and her home was about to be foreclosed on. The second time she did it was because she was bored, and the third time was because she "caught the bug".

characters.name: Gustin Tobin
characters.description: Beef and Brian's great-grandfather, and the Tobin children's great-great-grandfather, who was Lone Moose's first weatherman and also sold land to a meat company to dump meat into underground bunkers. Sins of Our Fathers: Beef discovers the name of his great-grandfather on the meat bunker blueprints, making him realize that he sold the land to the company and was responsible for the whole crisis that endured in the "For Whom the Smell Tolls Part 2". Sudden Name Change: His name was originally Rutger Tobin in his first mention in "For Whom the Smell Tolls Part 2". It was later changed to Gustin in "Anchor Ham Adventure". Wizard Classic: Ham's vision of his great-great-grandfather Gustin Tobin looks like a wizard, with a robe, along beard, and a weather vane for a staff. It's to the point Ham believes at first that he'sDumbledore, which Gustin admits is a good guess because he believes Dumbledore is based on him.

characters.name: Louis and Ruth Shaw
characters.description: The parents of Honeybee and Jerry, who run a curtain store in Fresno, California. Altar Diplomacy: They attempted to set Honeybee up with Calvin, so that they can combine their families' businesses when they take over. It doesn't work out, as Calvin and Honeybee areLike Brother and Sister. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: When Honeybee was 15 when she worked at the mall, she forgot her jacket so her dad came and used the mall intercom to tell her "Sweetie, it's Daddy, I'm here with your jackie". When she meets with her dad, he booped her nose in front of everyone and they laughed at her. Parents as People: While they may be workaholics with their curtain store, and pushy and embarrassing to their children, they are ultimately still loving parents who mean well for their kids.

characters.name: Jerry Shaw
characters.description: The younger brother of Honeybee. He moves up to Lone Moose to try and find a new path in life, and winds up dressing as Bigfoot at events round town. Big Little Brother: He's taller than Honeybee and is the same size as Wolf despite being younger than her. Cool Older Sibling-in-Law: Is this to the younger Tobins, especially Moon. Does Not Like Spam: Doesn't like crackers, as the mix of crunchy and bland "confuses his mouth". Dreaded Kids' Party Entertainer Job: Inverted. In "Game of Snownes Adventure," Honeybee mentions that with his Bigfoot costume, Jerry is blowing up on the kids' party circuit, enough so that he has money for headshots and a website.

characters.name: Granny Shaw
characters.description: Honeybee and Jerry's grandmother, and the mother of either Louis or Ruth. Accidental Misnaming: She calls Beef "Keith" and doesn't believe it's his real name. Ambiguously Related: We don't know if she's the mother of Ruth or Louis. Faking the Dead: At one of the previous Halloween parties, Granny Shaw faked her death and held her funeral during the party. When her family got close to her coffin, she popped out and announced that she was alive. While Honeybee and her parents had a good laugh at it, Jerry was completely scared and had a freak out. Out of Focus: She doesn't receive as much spotlight as the rest of the Shaw family.

characters.name: Delmer
characters.description: An elderlyYupikman and Tobin family friend. Catchphrase: "Oh hell no." Parental Substitute: Beef and Brian used to rely on him for help with their schoolwork and even lived with him while their parentsbriefly joined a space cult. He essentially raised Beef and Brian. Moon even called himself his "surrogate grandson" when having dinner with him once, and the whole family loves him enough to enjoy exaggerated bedtime stories about him. Despite this, none of the Tobins refer to him with a title and simply call him by his name, probably because he ultimately isn't an official part of the family tree. Senior Citizen's Even Older Parent: Despite being 80 years old, his father is still alive. Small Role, Big Impact: While Delmer does have a recurring presence throughout the show, his moments tend to be very brief, with "Wanted: Delmer Alive Adventure" being the exception. However, he's nonetheless had a major impact on Beef's life that ultimately shaped him into the man he is by the start of the show.

characters.name: Londra Pennypacker
characters.description: A fisherwoman who's usually seen at the docks. Butch Lesbian: Tall, stocky, typically wearing masculine-style fishing gear, and revealed in "Bear of Beeftown Adventure" to be interested in women. Phrase Catcher: When Wolf or Judy tells her they don't want to be bothered, they tell her "Not now, Londra!" and she happily complies. The Pollyanna: She's always happy no matter the situation. Like when Wolf and Judy telling her to not bother them or mentioning she's hosting a Tupperware party and she'll owe thousands of dollars to her mentor if she doesn't sell enough.

characters.name: Santiago Carpaccio
characters.description: A recurring character who appears in Lone Moose. He's quiet and rather mysterious. Ambiguously Jewish: In "Pa-shank Redemption Adventure", he is shown dropping a cake saying "Happy Adult Bar Mitzvah Santiago" implying he is converting to Judaism. Catchphrase: "It would be an honor". Girlfriend in Canada: A variant. In "Tasteful Noods Adventure", Santiago picks up a smoothie from Smoothie Boss that was supposed to be for a "Gloria". When Judy accuses him of "smoothie snatching", he says this: "Well, sometimes I just like to give a woman's name and pretend I'm picking up a smoothie for my imaginary wife." He is aware that this is perceived as kind of pathetic. Rouge Angles of Satin: Santiago accidentally ordered aSatancostume instead of aSantacostume for the white elephant party. He decides to roll with it by stuffing the belly and adding a white beard (much to Mayor Pepper's confusion).

characters.name: Old Jody Jr.
characters.description: A trader that everyone goes to when they need to get something that's difficult for them to obtain. Honest John's Dealership: He claims that if it exists, he can get it for you, except he rips everybody off and he will trade away your stuff even if you want a refund.Moon:Old Jody Jr. is always ripping everybody off 'cause he thinks he's the only game in town, and that's just because he's theonlygame in town.

characters.name: Dell
characters.description: A fisherwoman who's trying to get back into fishing and one of Beef'sLove Interests. The Bus Came Back: Returns every now and then sporadically in episodes focusing on Beef's love life. Cartwright Curse: The reason why Dell rejects going out with Beef is because she sees herself as cursed because her previous husbands died in horrific accidents and doesn't want him to die like them. Her first husband froze to death in their freezer ("He wasn't very bright"), the next two husbands died falling into holes, the fourth husband was in a plane crash and survivedbut was eaten by his friend, and her recent husband died in a fishing accident where a dock line wrapped around his neck, pulled him into the water, andthen popped his head clean off.

characters.name: Greta Meatweep
characters.description: A kind-hearted, somewhat eccentric woman who has a passion for poetry and bird-watching, and one of Beef’sLove Interests. Fictional Disability: ARunning Gagis every time she appears, she mentions having a fictional physical condition, most of the time as an excuse for her tardiness. Innocently Insensitive: After having a one-night stand with Beef, she writes a poem about it in the newspaper column and reveals Beef’s identity, unintentionally causing him embarrassment among the townspeople when everyone finds out a few days later. Love Interest: To Beef, with most of her appearances being in episodes centered on Beef’s love life. The Muse: Beef is often the subject for Greta’s romantic poems. In her debut, it was her who was the subject of Beef’s poem where he expresses his feelings for her.

characters.name: John Johnson
characters.description: The editor-in-chief ofThe Lone Moose Wind. Repetitive Name:JohnJohnson.

characters.name: Junkyard Kyle
characters.description: A woman who runs a junkyard. Ambiguously Gay: Despite appearing to be aButch Lesbian, her sexual orientation is unconfirmed and she even pretended to be Beef’s wife one time. Big Badass Rig: She has Mad Max-style rescue vehicle that took her a decade to build and she would later make modifications to it so she can cross the spoiled meat that's all over the ground and protect herself from the pizzlies in “For Whom The Smell Tolls”. Gender-Blender Name: Her name may be Kyle, but she's a woman. Quirky Girl, Quirky Tux: She wears a tuxedo at Wolf and Honeybee's wedding.

characters.name: Cheesecake
characters.description: The Alcoholic: He's a very heavy drinker despite his appearance. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Was originally the same height as Wolf, but as of Season 4, he is now shorter than Ham and Honeybee. Freaky Fashion, Mild Mind: Inverted. Cheesecake looks and dresses rather blandly, but he acts like a party animal, and any time that Wolf and Honeybee go drinking with him ends in utter mayhem. Insurance Fraud: His fiancée tried to kill him for the insurance money. He literally found a knife with his name on it under her pillow. Only Known by Their Nickname: Only ever referred to as Cheesecake, which is presumably not his real first name.

characters.name: Chief Edna
characters.description: The chief of police of Lone Moose and also the owner of the boatyard. Action Girl: Whilst Lone Moose doesn’t often see anything particularly serious, as the town’s main police officer, in the event of actual criminals it falls to Edna to handle them, and she is always up to the task (even if she doesn’t often carry her gun). Big Little Sister: She's slightly taller than her big sister, Chief Elba. Brains and Brawn: She has this sort of relationship with her sister Elba whenever they team up, being the Brain. Edna is noted to be the smarter of the two and normally formulates the plans for how they two go about it. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Much like most inhabitants of Lone Moose, Edna is pretty quirky with her at times coming across as close to playing a police officer as actually being one (such as her and her sister geeking out at her getting to order a criminal to come out and surrender, or admitting she only knows how to shoot due to watching a puppet teach the class), but make no mistake she is actually pretty good at her job. The few times the series requires her to face an actual criminal, she usually has little trouble handling them, despite admitting to regularly going around unarmed.

characters.name: Vera Warren
characters.description: One of the townsfolk. An old woman with an abrasive attitude. Dirty Old Woman: She admitted rather proudly that Skanky the Christmas Tree was turning her on. Grumpy Old Woman: Is rather irritable.

characters.name: Maude
characters.description: The owner of Maude’s All-Day Diner. Ambiguous Gender Identity: It’s heavily implied she’s transgender given her character design and the fact that her actress is trans. However, it’s never outright confirmed.

characters.name: Zelda Blop
characters.description: Beef’s stalker and ex-classmate from high school. Bait-and-Switch: After Beef tells Zelda he's not going to marry her, she reveals she spent so much money on her wedding dress by getting a reverse mortgage and selling an organ, which shocks the Tobins. But Zelda reveals she sold her mother's organ she played in the church for years before she died, which shocks the Tobins again. But Zelda reveals that her motherdyedher hair blonde and became a real floozy so the church kicked her out. Black Widow: Zelda is just crazy enough to kill her own fiancée to get married to Beef. Blatant Lies: Zelda claims that she is happily engaged with Ribeye and has no intention of pursuing Beef any longer, but she blatantly keeps doing so. Childhood Marriage Promise: Zelda and Beef had a pact in high school that if neither one was married by age 40 they would get married. Now it's Zelda's 40th birthday and she comes to Beef's house in a wedding dress, fully expecting that Beef will keep his side of the pact.

characters.name: Looney Louie
characters.description: An odd resident of Lone Moose who only speaks in riddles. Cloud Cuckoolander: Is rather… eccentric. Delighting in Riddles: Looney Louie is an oddball who typically speaks in riddles. When Mayor Peppers ask Louie if he knows where the bad smell is coming from, he admits he knows but he only decides to tell them in riddles. When Beef and Moon meet Louie at his house to ask him more about the bad smell, he only tells them in riddles again. But when he sees that they're bad at guessing his riddles, he gives up and straight up tells them about the meat bunkers all over Lone Moose. Although, he does admit he was paid to keep quiet about the meat bunkers. Who Names Their Kid "Dude"?: His real name is in fact Looney, short for Loonjamin.

characters.name: Noodie the Noodle
characters.description: The mascot forMomma Poppa’s Italian Restaurant–an unidentified man in an uncanny noodle suit who inexplicably only has one arm. The Bus Came Back: He returns in Season 4 appearing at a bonfire alongside the other town mascots. Creepy Mascot Suit: A very uncanny looking noodle mascot with only one arm who acts hostile to Ham. Dance Sensation: The end credits song for “Tasteful Noods Adventure” is about Noodie doing the dance called "The Noodie". Destroy the Evidence: After Ham takes pictures of Momma and Poppa's food practice as evidence to expose them using his phone, Noodie snatches his phone, runs off, and shows it to Momma and Poppa. After Ham refuses to keep Momma and Poppa's disgusting food practices a secret, Momma drops his phone in boiling pasta sauce and Noodie literally pushes him out of the restaurant.

characters.name: Potato Patty
characters.description: A woman in a potato costume and a work acquaintance of Jerry's. Brick Joke: On the way to Dick Chateau's, Jerry says that something is "Po-TAY-to, Po-TOT-o". Potato Patty gets mad and claims that saying is stupid because nobody has ever pronounced it "Po-TOT-oh". When the trio finally meet Dick Chateau, Dick calls her "Po-TOT-oh Patty". Handy Mouth: Because Potato Patty's potato costume limits her arm movements, she got really good using her mouth as a substitute, such as using her mouth to open doors and untying herself from her sack. Ode to Food: The end credits song in her single appearance is about Potato Patty singing about giving potatoes out during Christmas.

characters.name: Dick Chateau
characters.description: The richest man in Lone Moose. Collector of the Strange: Since he's forbidden to hunt real animals, Dick Chateau resorts to hunting and collecting mascot costumes. Cool Boat: His yacht, theFloating Dick, which is decked out with multiple amenities, including a tuxedo dispenser, a bowling alley and several "cocaine decks". Even Beef is impressed, at least by how well it steers. A Dick in Name:Played Withand Lampshaded. Both of the Chateau brothers are named Richard, but respectively go by Dick and Rick. Beef and Brian point out the irony in the one whodoesn'tgo by Dick being the bigger dick. Egomaniac Hunter: Dick Chateau was a big game hunter who travelled all over Alaska hunting the animals until Game Warden Burt forbid him from hunting them due to killing some endangered species. Dick was bored until he saw the mascot for the Polar Bear panini shop. He suddenly desired to take the costume and started collecting mascot costumes ever since.

characters.name: Rick Chateau
characters.description: Dick’s brother, who is also named Richard. A Dick in Name:Played Withand Lampshaded. Both of the Chateau brothers are named Richard, but respectively go by Dick and Rick. Beef and Brian point out the irony in the one whodoesn'tgo by Dick being the bigger dick. A Family Affair: Dick's wife, Tatyana, cheated on him by doing the "German Squirmin'" with his brother Rick in front on himin a car on a roller coaster. Jerk with a Heart of Jerk: Rick Chateau acts genial at first, but it's just an act. He orchestrated the entire wedding to hurt his brother by marrying his ex-wife. Rick sadistically reveals it right as Dick starts apologizing for ever intending to screw with the wedding, rubbing salt in the wound.

characters.name: Joe Dinkum
characters.description: Dirt’s childhood friend whom she was forbidden from seeing by her parents as a girl. Joe had an unrequited crush on Dirt as kids. Did You Die?: After Moon and his friends bring Joe to Dirt and she explains her history with him and reveals at the end she burned down their rocket fort, Russell asks if she burnt Joe alive, but Henry points out that Joe is literally stand next to them, and Russell admits to have forgotten that. Incompatible Orientation: When Joe Dinkum is brought to Aunt Dirt to sort out their fight Joe eventually explains it stemmed from his crush on her at the time. When Dirt told her father the idea of kissing any of her friends was gross Joe felt slighted and stood her up for their play date. When Dirt explains that she’s a lesbian and it wasn't personal, Joe says the reason doesn’t matter, she shouldn’t have to kiss anyone she doesn’t want to and the two repair their friendship. Nice Guy: Joe Dinkum has become a pleasant old man with a lot of emotional intelligence. He openly acknowledges that the fight from several decades ago was started by his immaturity (even if Dirt didoverreact) and apologizes. Petty Childhood Grudge: For decades, Dirt held a grudge against Joe Dinkum and his friends for replacing her in their friend group. When Moon, Henry, and Russell unintentionally did this to her, Dirt's grudge is reawakened and she takes it out on them. Moon and his friends get Joe to meet with Dirt and once she sees him, she immediately tries to kill him. After Joe explains his reason for leaving her and apologizes for his actions, Dirt drops her grudge and forgives all four of them.

characters.name: Principal Gibbons
characters.description: The principal of Lone Moose School. Putting the "Pal" in Principal: Is pretty well-liked by the student body, not to mention rarely punishes the kids unless he absolutely has to. Reasonable Authority Figure: In "Period Piece Adventure", he's actually very interested in the final protest piece and has questions about the symbolism. He also explains to the group that the school actually gets a kickback for using the old sanitary belts, and that money pays for things like the art supplies Judy was going to use for the mural. He agrees to use some of this money to put tampons in the girls’ bathroom in the future.

characters.name: Mr. Golovkin
characters.description: One of Judy and Ham's teachers. A Day in the Limelight: He gets focused on in "Arranger-ous Minds Adventure" and we learn more about his life, including how he has OCD. Everybody Knew Already: He's in a "secret relationship" with Ms. Anderson, but Principal Gibbons and the rest of the school staff already knows about their relationship and questions why they're trying to keep it a secret when everybody is happy for them. In "Arranger-ous Minds Adventure", the rest of the students already know about their relationship after one of them caught them kissing and told everyone. Growing Up Sucks: He bluntly tells Judy that becoming an adult isn't as great she thought it would be because you'll eventually have to deal with many disappointments in your life. Jerkass Realization: In "Arranger-ous Minds Adventure", after he tells Moon that he'll die alone if he likes organizing stuff, Moon realizes that he has OCD like him and plans to move in with him because they're freaks no woman would ever love. After Moon tells him how he has a crush on Quinn and she made fun of him for organizing trash, Golovkin realizes that Moon is afraid he's like him and as a teacher he should not have told a student like Moon that he's going to die alone. He reluctantly agrees to try to change his way so he can make Moon feel better about himself and hope to get back together with Ms. Anderson.

characters.name: Ms.McNamara
characters.description: The guidance counselor of Lone Moose School. Adults Are Useless: She's a lousy guidance counselor and play director. In "Stools Rush in Adventure", despite Judy's experience in musicals and Chrissy not being a good singer,McNaramacasts Chrissy as the female lead and Judy as Chrissy's understudy and a bar stool because she wants to help Chrissy get out of her comfort zone and have a chance to shine, despite Chrissy's protest that she can't sing and never wanted the lead role, and thinks Judy is anAttention Whorewho talks too much. Her attempts at helping Chrissy only makes both of the girls miserable and humiliated. Amelia, Judy, and Chrissy all thinks she's a lousy guidance counselor. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing:Not that she hides it very well, but in "Stools Rush in Adventure", you'd think that being a guidance counselor would make Ms.McNaramakind and understanding to the students, but no. Instead, she gives Judy two humiliating roles seemingly just because she personally doesn't like Judy while forcing Chrissy to take the female lead even though Chrissy is unable to sing and is deeply uncomfortable with the part. If that weren't enough, she bad mouths Judy to Chrissy in private. Kick the Dog: In "Stools Rush in Adventure", when it's clear that Chrissy can't sing on stage and she doesn't want the female lead role, the reasonable thing for Ms.McNamarato do is have Judy replace her since she's her understudy; but instead she decides to have Judy sing Chrissy's lines from the pit and have Chrissy lip sync it on stage. She even tells Judy to wear a hat when she's in the pit because people tend to throw their gum down there. Unusual Pets for Unusual People: She has a pet weasel. When her original one dies, Judy bribes her with anew onein an attempt to get her to give her a letter of recommendation for a summer program.

characters.name: Ms. Anderson
characters.description: One of the teachers at Lone Moose School and Mr. Golovkin’s long-term girlfriend.—- Auto-Incorrect: When Mr. Golovkin texted Ms. Anderson to apologize for driving her away, he apologizes again after his auto-correct changed his original text to "I'm horny. Penis forgive me". Everybody Knew Already: She's in a "secret relationship" with Mr. Golovkin, but Principal Gibbons and the rest of the school staff already knows about their relationship and questions why they're trying to keep it a secret when everybody is happy for them. In "Arranger-ous Minds Adventure", the rest of the students already know about their relationship after one of them caught them kissing and told everyone. Forgotten Anniversary: Mr. Golovkin forgot his one-year anniversary with Ms. Anderson. Satellite Love Interest: Is basically aFlat Characterwith not much known about her other than her relationship with Mr. Golovkin or the fact that she’s a teacher. Furthermore, we don’t even know what grade or subject she teaches.

characters.name: Ms. Hill
characters.description: Moon, Henry, Russel, Debbie, and Quinn’s 5th grade teacher.—- Adults Are Useless: She does absolutely nothing to stop her class from heckling the students who have to give their speech to them, even if they're crying from their heckling. Apathetic Teacher: Downplayed; while she’s more of aFlat Characterwho doesn’t receive much screen-time or focus, her on-screen moments show her talking in a tired-sounding monotone and imply she’s tired of her students’ antics. Reasonable Authority Figure: She allows Moon to pass math from an F to a D- by allowing him to apply mathematics to his knowledge of outdoor activities.

characters.name: Gloria
characters.description: The lunchlady at Lone Moose and Dirt'sLove Interest. Birds of a Feather: She's equally as crazy and batty as Dirt, to the point of also having a secret weapons bunker. Butch Lesbian: Like Dirt, she's a gruff, masculine lunch lady.

characters.name: Crispin Cienfuegos
characters.description: A new student who works at Smoothie Boss in the Lone Moose Mall. He begins dating Ham late in Season One, but they break up early in Season 5. Accidental Misnaming: He kept misnaming Judy as Rudy in his first few appearances.. Alliterative Name:CrispinCienfuegos. Birds of a Feather: Crispin and Ham are both eccentric, and odd, butincredibly sweet boys, so it's unsurprising that they hit it off quickly and end up becoming a couple. Hidden Depths: "Bee's All That Adventure" reveals that he has the highest G.P.A. in his grade.

characters.name: Gill Beavers
characters.description: Judy's best platonic male friend who has an unrequited crush on her. Complexity Addiction: His plan to kiss Judy at the dance features 98 steps. Everyone Can See It: Everybody in their friend group knows he has a crush on Judy. They even talk about it in front of Gill and Judy in "Skidmark Holmes Adventure." I'm Standing Right Here: Claims he's so generic and beneath notice that hegot away with switching the pizza out for his grandma's underwearin "Skidmark Holmes Adventure." However,The Revealthathe was working with Kima to do socasts some doubt on it. Just Friends: He's Judy's "best platonic male friend" who she usually invites to the dance. Gill seems to have a crush on her, but she only sees him as a friend. Shedidkiss him one time when he flattered her enough, but that's all that's come of it.

characters.name: Bethany Bupatutti
characters.description: One of Judy's classmates. Emotionless Girl: Played with. She speaks with a very monotone, semi-bored-sounding voice, but still participates in voluntary activities with the other students and occasionally smiles. Establishing Character Moment: Her first line in her first appearance in "Pride and Prejudance Adventure" sets up exactlywhat kind of characterBethany will be.Principal Gibbons: Ladies, you'll now step forward to invite your dates in.Bethany: Whatever. The simulation makes our decisions anyway. Hates Their Parent: Bethany abhors spending literally any designated extended time with her unseen parents. In particular, being "threatened" with a family dinner by her mother prompted her to secretly squat in the school at night for a stretch of many days. Nightmare Fetishist: She's really interested in dark and creepy things.

characters.name: Drama John
characters.description: A student who likes seeing drama and being dramatic. Brutal Honesty: He is not afraid to speak his mind, and often does so for the sake of drama. Drama Queen: He likes drama and doing dramatic things. In "Period Piece Adventure", he only joined Judy's art project so he could storm out of it. Odd Friendship: Though it takes time for the show to establish it, he's best friends with Bethany. They're often seen together, but appear enough individually too much to count asThose Two Guys.

characters.name: Steven Huang
characters.description: One of Judy's classmates and potential love interests. Out of Focus: Hasn't had many major roles since Season 3. Romantic False Lead: Though he's set up as a love interest to Judy, it ultimately goes nowhere and he ends up dating Chrissy.

characters.name: Kima Evanoff
characters.description: Judy's best friend who is an Alaska Native. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Kima originally had a thin and slim body in the first two seasons, but as of Season 3's "Bee's All That Adventure" she now has a wider body frame more like her mother. Sudden Name Change: Went from Kima Brewper in the first two seasons to Kima Evanoff in Season 3's "Rear Genius Adventure."

characters.name: Quay
characters.description: The resident cool kid of Lone Moose School who plays the guitar. Sleeves Are for Wimps: Often seen wearing a sleeveless shirt with a sleeveless jacket on top of it.

characters.name: Amelia
characters.description: Judy's new friend who was previously homeschooled. Deadpan Snarker: She tends to be very sarcastic when she talks. Homeschooled Kids: Was homeschooled by her mother because she didn't want her daughter to be around "so many white kids", but was sent to regular school after her mother tried teaching her trigonometry. Quirky Girl, Quirky Tux: She wears a dark pink one to prom in "For Whom the Smell Tolls." Sassy Black Woman: Is rather sarcastic and blunt with her dialogue.

characters.name: Stacy B.
characters.description: Judy's ex-best friend who ditched her once she became popular and started bullying Judy. Alpha Bitch: She's one of the popular kids in Judy's grade and she's always making fun of Judy, along with her friends due to their association with Judy. Evil Is Petty: After ditching Judy as her best friend and hanging out with the cool kids, she doesn't just make fun of her, but she purposely ruins any of Judy's plans.While she doesn't have any beef with Kima and Amelia, she only makes fun of them because they're friends with Judy.In "Skidmark Holmes Adventure", she's aware of Judy's murder mystery party coming up so she purposely throws her party on the same day, making people from Judy's party choose to go to her party.In "Bee's All That Adventure", after Judy and her friends help make Jill cooler and everyone in school starts seeing Judy and her friends as cool, Stacy B. comes in and steals Jill away from her. While she doesn't have any beef with Kima and Amelia, she only makes fun of them because they're friends with Judy. In "Skidmark Holmes Adventure", she's aware of Judy's murder mystery party coming up so she purposely throws her party on the same day, making people from Judy's party choose to go to her party.

characters.name: Jill Gerbert-Erble
characters.description: The exchange student from the Lower 48 Exchange in “Bee’s All That Adventure” who is obsessed with bees. Judy attempts to befriend her to get back at Stacy B.. Cloud Cuckoolander: Jill is obsessed with bees, due to being raised on a bee farm. She eats honey with everything, talks nonstop about bees, and at some point she apparently tried to sting someone. Makeover Montage: Judy and her friends makeover Jill so she looks more normal, exchanging her bee-themed clothes for a plain yellow sweater. During the montage, the song is saying you should always be yourself, but if you're acting like a bee, then you should definitely be something else.

characters.name: Loud Sandy
characters.description: Judy's very loud classmate and friend. Break Them by Talking: In "Can't Hardly Debate Adventure", Aunt Dirt (posing as a lunchlady) guilts her into backing down from complaining about her cold pizza by making up a fake sob story about her past. Later, during theTraining Montage, Sandy asks a cafeteria lady for three brownies and when told it's one per kid she starts bothering the woman with facts about brownies until she gives her the entire tray just to make her leave. Cargo Ship: In "Dial M for Moon-der Adventure" a video was leaked of her marrying herself to aSkibidi Toiletfigure. Gasshole: She can burp on cue, as demonstrated in "Can't Hardly Debate Adventure" when she's pretending to be drunk. NO INDOOR VOICE: She's constantly yelling and has been banned from the school library because of this.

characters.name: Cool Mike
characters.description: The resident cool teen of Lone Moose and Judy’s ex-boyfriend. Big Jerk on Campus: While his dickish tendencies are more subtle and less visible, he’s nonetheless shallow and afraid to be associated with people he perceives as “uncool”. Cool Kid-and-Loser Friendship: Or rather Cool Kid and Loser Couple. He dates the nerdy Judy but only in secret as he fears it would damage his cool reputation. Instant Humiliation: Just Add YouTube!: How Judy gets back at him for being a douchebag of a boyfriend. Laser-Guided Karma: Judy gets back at him by humiliating him on herTikTokvideo series, thus ruining his cool reputation.

characters.name: Henry Tuntley
characters.description: One of Moon's friends. Dork in a Sweater: A precocious, geeky 10 year old kid in a green sweater vest. Not So Above It All: Despite seeming to be precocious and the most mature of Moon's friends, he still joins them in doing stupid things and is less mature than Moon in "Bust A Moon Adventure" to the point where Moon has to parent him. Practically Different Generations: "Rear Genius Adventure" reveals that Henry has at least one sibling who's old enough to have children of their own. However, this unseen sibling never appears on-screen and is only briefly mentioned. Sleepwalking: Henry has a habit of sleeptunneling. It gets worse after he's seen scary movies, in spite of his denial.

characters.name: Russell
characters.description: One of Moon's friends. As You Know: Russell always refers to Jamie as "my mom's boyfriend Jamie", even when talking to Moon and other friends who already knows who he is. Disappeared Dad: His biological father is never mentioned, and given that Russel wishes Jamie was his real dad, it’s likely he’s not in the picture. Good Stepfather: His mother's boyfriend, Jamie, apparently. Russell absolutelyadoreshim, and keeps finding ways to bring him up in conversations. Kiddie Kid: Still likes to be told bedtime stories and gets scared when stuck on top of a one-foot high toddler slide.

characters.name: Debbie Van
characters.description: A classmate of Moon who's popular in his grade. Abusive Offspring: Even her own mother is afraid of Debbie, and Debbie used to even call her by her name. Alpha Bitch: She's an eleven-year-old version. She's the most talented and beautiful girl in Moon's grade, and also the meanest. Creepy Child: And how. Whenever she is even slightly embarrassed, she takes it to theextreme (something the school staff found out the hard way). Disappeared Dad: Her father is never brought up and his status is unknown.

characters.name: Quinn Notti
characters.description: A girl who Moon has a crush on that, in return, reciporicates his crush. She becomes a part of his friend group as of "Autumn if You've Got' Em Adventure". Bait-and-Switch: She rejects Moon’s offer to be his date to their practice prom in “Aunt Misbehavin’ Adventure” because she already has a date, but it turns out to just be her pet pig. She and Moon end up dancing together in the end. Granola Girl: Shares Moon’s interest in animals and the outdoors. Housepet Pig: She has a pot-bellied pig named David, who is her practice date to the Lil Prepper’s Practice Prom. Nice Girl: UnlikeAlpha BitchDebbie who bullies Moon and his friends, Quinn is kind-hearted and agreeable with Moon.

characters.name: Calm Callum
characters.description: Loud Sandy’s little brother who, as his name implies, is quiet and relaxed. Establishing Character Moment: His introduction shows him sitting at a lunch table by himself in aPrayer Posewhile holding a feather. Improbable Age: Downplayed; despite being the same age as Moon and his friends, he’s the instructor of a meditation class. Not impossible per se, but definitely on the younger side. Mellow Fellow: Is relaxed and reserved, even while at school. Sibling Yin-Yang: Is rather quiet and meek in comparison to his sister Loud Sandy, who’s loud enough to the point of being banned from the school library.

characters.name: Dorothy Tuntley
characters.description: Henry’s mom, who is a family friend of the Tobins. The Alcoholic: She’s a rather heavy drinker during social scenes. Alcohol-Induced Idiocy: Dorothy Tuntley would get drunk during their hockey games and will do things that will get her sent to the penalty box, like harassing the referee multiple times. Cloud Cuckoolander: Is a little... out there. Naked People Are Funny: When Honeybee is interim mayor and temporarily legalizes everything in Lone Moose, Dorothy can be seen naked riding on the back of the moose with wine in one hand.

characters.name: Jim Tuntley
characters.description: Dorothy’s husband and Henry’s dad. Henpecked Husband: Implied, as whenever he’s shown with his wife, she does all the talking while he remainsThe Quiet One.

characters.name: Esther Evanhoff
characters.description: Kima’s mother and Walt’s wife, who is a smokejumper. Jerkass Ball: Despite being rather percipient in most of her appearances, she’s uncharacteristically selfish towards her daughter and Judy in "Barrel Be Blood Adventure" when they sign up to be junior smokejumpers. Basically, she forces them to do a bunch of chores and clean up after the smokecrew, who are living likeLazyBums. It’s no wonder why Judy and Kima were the only ones to sign up for the program. Only Sane Woman: She is one of the more level-headed and reasonable resident’s of Lone Moose. In “Bee’s All That Adventure”, she gives Judy, Kima, and Amelia some really wise and insightful advice about friendships and high-school popularity.

characters.name: Walt Evanhoff
characters.description: Kima’s father and Esther’s husband, who is an environmental scientist. Atypical Team-Up Episode: "MIB: Men in Belts Adventure" focuses on him and Beef becoming best friends until a feud causes them to get apart from each other... all for a belt. Incredibly Lame Fun: Beef and Walt bond over such activities as looking at construction sites, watching trains go by and bird watching. Their children find all these things boring and are glad that their dads have someone to do them with so they wouldn't have to. OOC Is Serious Business: Walt is an environmental scientist who typically does the best he can to take care of the earth, but he’s so desperate to have the Evanoffs win in “Rear Genius Adventure” that he’s willing to put on poisonous metal paint and wash it off in the river to avoid its side effects. Poor Communication Kills: When Walt steals Beef’s train belt, Walt’s only excuse is that it’s “his” belt, causing their feud to get worse. After their kids force them to talk to each other, Walt explains that Kathleen stole that belt from him around the time Ham was born. When Beef askswhy Walt didn’t just explain that in the first place, Walt says he knew how much the belt meant to Beef and he didn’t want to upset him by knowing Kathleen stole that gift for him. Beef allows Walt to have the belt, repairing their friendship.

characters.name: Dane Evanhoff
characters.description: Walt’s nephew and Kima’s cousin, who is a 19-year-old college student. He lives with his aunt and uncle. From Cousin to Honorary Sibling: Because Dane lives with his cousin Kima, they are more like brother and sister. Nephewism: Dane appears to be living with his Aunt Esther and Uncle Walt, with no mention of his parents’ whereabouts. Perma-Stubble: Has a bit of stubble on his upper-lip, though not a full beard. Sibling Rivalry: Kima and Dane bicker like a brother and sister would, such as when Kima calls him nasty, he tells her she mispronounced “extremely cool”

characters.name: Carissa Van
characters.description: Debbie’s mom and Beef’s girlfriend fromS 4 E 08"Bear of Beeftown Adventure" untilS 5 E 09"Dial M for Moon-der Adventure". Adults Are Useless: A case ofEarly-Installment Weirdness. In Season 2, even though she’s aware of Debbie planning on beating up Moon, she never intervenes to stop it, mainly because she’s afraid of her own daughter. Ascended Extra: Gets a lot more focus in late Season 4 due to starting a romantic relationship with Beef. Crush Blush: Beef and Carissa are shown blushing a couple of times when they start showing attraction towards each other. Good Parents: Is genuinely loving and caring towards her daughter Debbie, in spite of her bad attitude.

characters.name: Marie
characters.description: Struggling Single Mother: Subverted. While she admits being a single mother has its challenges, her boyfriend Jamie has helped tremendously and stepped up as a father figure for Russel. Woman Scorned: After Beef reveals to Carissa that Chumbo is cheating on her, Marie and Dorothy wants to get back at Chumbo and wants to kill him but Beef offers a more sensible solution: putting his snowmobile inside a small dumpster and filling it with water so by the time Chumbo finds his snowmobile it will be encased in a giant ice cube.

characters.name: Jamie
characters.description: Marie’s long-term boyfriend whom Russel deeply adores. Good Stepfather: Russel isobsessedwith Jamie to the point of bringing him up in every conversation. Given that we never see Jamie outside of a credits scene where he has no speaking roles, it’s unclear if Jamie is objectively as great as Russel says he is. Elegant Classical Musician: Him playing the flute is just another thing Russel admires about him. Russel is even Jamie’s self-proclaimed flute caddy.

characters.name: Rustle
characters.description: Russel's younger cousin and Marie's nephew. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Rustle might seem at first like the gentlest soul to ever grace God's green Earth, but with him giving Moon a menacing smirk while getting a hug from Russel, Moon and the audience quickly find out his true colors as an apex predator. Entertainment Above Their Age: While Moon and Russel enjoy watching horror movies, Russel and Rustle enjoy watching the works of Dianne Wiest. Incredibly Lame Fun: Rustle suggests to Moon and Russel to playEtymology Trail, a game where someone picks a word from the bowl, and then everyone tries to break it down to its most basic roots using a dictionary. Moon doesn't seem to be amused. My Nayme Is: Russel's cousin is named Rustle, which sounds exactly the same, causing some confusion when Moon asks for Russel and Rustle comes as well.

characters.name: Alyson Lefebvrere
characters.description: The manager of Point & Shoot Photography Studio and Judy's boss, and Beef’s first and mainLove Interest. LOL, 69: She flirts with Beef by pointing out that the total of his purchase ends with sixty-nine cents. Oblivious to Love: Early on, Beef was oblivious to Alyson’s obvious hints of flirtation. He eventually picks up on it in Season 3 and has even kissed her multiple times. Out of Focus: She was in almost every episode in the first 2 seasons. But by Season 4, only had lines inone episode.The Bus Came Back: In the fifth season episode "Serendipi-Beef Adventure", she is shown again, and shares a kiss with Beef. The Bus Came Back: In the fifth season episode "Serendipi-Beef Adventure", she is shown again, and shares a kiss with Beef.

characters.name: Holden
characters.description: A 17-year-old community college student and fellow coworker of Judy’s, as well as her ex-boyfriend. Bookworm: Part of the reason him and Judy click is his sophistication and love of classic literature. Grade Skipper: A variant; he’s 17 and already in community college, but only because he has a G.E.D.. Hipster: Holden is a 2010s version, having pretentious taste in books and movies and liberal political views (Judy's imagined version of their future together includes them owning a hybrid car but mostly biking everywhere). Incredibly Lame Fun: Judy and Holden's "first dates" include going to thecuckoo clock store at the moment when all the cuckoo clocks go off at once, and visiting the place where they throw out all the misshapen corndogs at All Corndogs Go to Tummy.Alanis: So he... took you to a trash can?

characters.name: Granville Teners
characters.description: The conductor of the kiddie train at the mall and Mr. Golovkin’s rival. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: According to Judy, Granville Tenders seems like a really nice guy. However, Mr. Golovkin states that Granville stole the caboose of his mall train from Golovkin's porch when it was delivered to him, and during the heist, Granville proudly brags about how he stole it, not even trying to deny it. Rail Enthusiast: Much like Mr. Golovkin, he owns a mall train and is a train fanatic in general.

characters.name: Mayor Peppers
characters.description: The mayor of Lone Moose. Humble Goal: All Mayor Peppers wants on his one day off (besides peace between the Tobins, Evanoffs, and Tuntleys) is to eat a weed gummy and hang out in the bouncy castle.

characters.name: Councilman Roy
characters.description: One of three Lone Moose City Councilpeople and Toby the Eagle's owner. Reasonable Authority Figure: Councilman Roy & Toby defends the Tobins & Shaws from Mayor Folly by pointing out that the bear is being kept illegally on his property, as he does not have the necessary paperwork. He asks Mayor Folly to forget this incident so that he will also forget the lack of paperwork.

characters.name: Councilperson Gwen
characters.description: One of three Lone Moose City Councilpeople. Handy Feet: Because Roy and Toby hold 2/3 majority of the city council, Councilperson Gwen just gave up and spends council meetings practicing picking things up with her feet. At the next council meeting, Gwen can be seen trying to solve a rubik's cube with her feet. Judy mentions she once ran into Gwen at the mall food court, where she was able to eat an entire serving of lo mein while operating the chopsticks with her toes.

characters.name: Toby the Eagle
characters.description: The third member of Lone Moose City Council who is also Roy's pet eagle. Artistic License – Animal Care: InReal Life, keeping an eagle in captivity is illegal in the US, especially because Toby started as a non-rescue wild bird and was not captive-bred. Additionally, he’s frequently shown perching on Roy’s shoulders, which is very dangerous as birds of prey tend to go for human eyes, not to mention the fact that their claws can severely cut through human skin, and neither Roy nor any of his handlers are ever shown using the proper gloves or equipment required to handle him. Caligula's Horse: Is an eagle and a member of City Council. It's apparently very common for animals to hold government positions in Alaska; a guinea pig was once assistant governor and town of Talkeetna had a cat named "Catt Damon" for their mayor (the latter of which ispartially true inReal Life). Feathered Fiend: Is known to antagonize residents he doesn’t like, such as when he pushed Beef into a fountain, got Beef’s favorite frozen yogurt parlor closed down and replaced with aneagle paraphernalia store, and when he stole Honeybee’s scarf. Pet Monstrosity: Eagles are very aggressive and dangerous predators inReal Lifeand should not be handled by humans in captivity. Even Beef lampshades this in an episode where Moon is entrusted to look after Toby.

characters.name: Diondra Tundra
characters.description: A news reporter for the local news of Lone Moose. The Bus Came Back: After not having had a notable role since early Season 2, she finally returns in Season 5's "Anchor Ham Adventure" due to the episode primarily taking place at the news station. Nepotism: Her nephew is hired as another high-school intern alongside Ham but never does any work and isalways on his phone not wanting to be bothered. Despite his bad attitude, the rest of the news station won't fire him due to his ties with her. Rhyming Names: Her name rhymes.

characters.name: Harry Hotfog
characters.description: A local celebrity and the weather forecaster of Lone Moose. Mr. Fanservice:In-Universe; is noted to be quite the looker. Plot Allergy: Harry Hotfog has a dairy allergy and can only have oatmilk in his coffee. When Ham gives the other intern coffee with real milk to give to Harry, it makes Harry's face swell up andstart burping and farting uncontrollably. Small Name, Big Ego: Is rather cocky due to the fame and status that his job gives him. Younger Than They Look: When Moon is convinced Harry is his biological father, he’s immediately ruled out once he reveals he’s only 23 despite having grey hair. Apparently, Harry dyes his hair gray so his coworkers will take him seriously.

characters.name: Vince the Cloud Guy
characters.description: TheGreen Screenguy at the weather station whose job is to move the clouds while Harry forecasts the weather. Asshole Victim: At the end of his debut episode, everything seems to have worked out alright (with Harry even agreeing to let Ham continue helping out at the station from time to time) after everyone there admits to letting their weather ambitions get the better of them, but Vince appears to still be out of a job, with no word on if he was able to get a new green suit and be rehired. However, considering how unpleasant he was, abusing his small amount of power to be a jerk to Ham during the latter's internship, it’s hard to feel sorry for him. Chroma Key: His entire job. Geek Physique: To highlight Harry beingAlways Someone Betterto him, Vince has a scrawny physique with a potbelly sticking out, not to mention being balding, in contrast to Harry’s good looks. Green-Eyed Monster: Is jealous of all the spotlight given to Harry to the point of being an absoluteJerkassand is waiting anxiously to replace him one day.

characters.name: Mayor Ted Folly IV
characters.description: The mayor of Lone Moose’s rival town Ted’s Folly. Disguised in Drag: Mayor Ted Folly disguised himself as a British woman named Barbara Baconbottom who moved into Lone Moose for two months so he can infiltrate the Rear Gifts Festival to enter the Turd Drop and cheat to win so he can ruin Mayor Peppers' day-off. Hair-Trigger Temper: Has a rather short temper and tolerance for pranks against himself or his town. Pungeon Master: Mayor Folly loves to use puns in his speech.Mayor: In light of Teddy's disappearance we're considering canceling today's Bear-Athlon for the first time in its 100-year history. I just can'tbearthe thought of breaking the hearts of all of today'spaw-ticipants, it's toogrizzly. And my motorcycle is also missing, I am bothrevved upabout it andwheely-wheelysad. Small Town Rivalry: Lone Moose has a rivalry with the town of Ted's Folly that originated 150 years ago when the wife of the Lone Moose's mayor threw a stuffed beaver at the wife of Ted's Folly's mayor leading to bad blood. This has caused the two towns to taunt & prank each other.

characters.name: Chief Elba
characters.description: Little Big Sister: She's slightly shorter than her little sister, Chief Edna. Police Are Useless: Zig-Zagged. In "Say It Again, Ham Adventure", she and Chief Edna don't actually carry their guns with them (instead keeping them in their glove compartments), so they are laughably unprepared when Beef's cousin, Danica, pulls a gun on them. However, they are able to successfullyDistract and Disarmher. Sibling Team: When she’s in town with her sister, Chief Edna, they will usually work together to back each other up.

characters.name: Principal Bowtie
characters.description: The principal of Juneau Horse Prep and Principal Gibbons' longtime rival. My Rule Fu Is Stronger than Yours: Principal Bowtie uses the rules to gets Lone Moose disqualified for Dirt not being technically employed by the school, but Judy uses the rules against him and his team when she finds a rule that allows Dirt to replace the team since she never finished high school so she's still technically a student. During the debate, the team helps Dirt win by preventing Bowtie Jr. from making his points by disrupting him from the audience since there's no rules about audience members disrupting the debaters since they never needed it. As a result, after Lone Moose wins, the judge for the Debate Tournament lets them know that next year they're going to do a thorough overhaul of the rules to avoid another situation like this. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: Has been Principal Gibbons’ rival since college. Upper-Class Twit: Makes his wealth status and that of his school no secret to Gibbons and his students.

characters.name: Eli
characters.description: Kima’s date to prom. A tuba player with a large Adam’s apple.

characters.name: Laird
characters.description: Judy’s date to prom. A tall 6’7” teen boy.

characters.name: Alanis Morissette
characters.description: Judy's imaginary friend and inspiration she sees in the northern lights. Amazing Technicolor Population: Because she's made of the northern lights, her color palette isn't bound by human limitations. Her skin is a transparent blue, blending in with the sky behind her. As Herself: The real Alanis lends her voice to her character in the show. Imaginary Real Person: She's anImaginary Friendto Judy in the form of northern lights, but modelled on the real Alanis Morissette. Not-So-Imaginary Friend: Occasionally she will continue to talk even after Judy has left the scene.

characters.name: Tusk Johnson
characters.description: A former mountain man who used to have his own TV show, "Tusk Johnson Mountain Man". Absurdly Elderly Mother: He knocked up his fiance camerawoman Doris despite her being 53. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Hasn't appeared or even been mentioned since Season 2. Feel No Pain: Tusk suffered through so much hypothermia that he can't feel anything in his left upper thigh and has Moon stab his left leg with a fork to prove it. Hedoesfeel pain when Moon stabs the wrong leg. Heel–Face Turn: In his first appearance in "Tusk in the Wind Adventure," Tusk freeloads off the Tobins, tries to poach endangered eagle eggs, and nearly gets Wolf killed/seriously injured. In his second appearance in "From Tusk 'Til Dawn Adventure," Tusk apologizes for his actions and claims he's turned over a new leaf. Though Beef thinks he's lying for most of the episode, Tusk ultimately is trying to do better and works with the Tobinsto defeat the people that took Beef's boat and stranded Tusk's bachelor party guests in the ocean.

characters.name: 16 Swedish Sisters
characters.description: Judy’s favorite Swedish pop band, which consist of 16 sisters. Always Identical Twins: Most of the sets of triplets appear to be identical, with the only thing differentiating them being their hairstyles. Band of Relatives: The Sixteen Swedish Sisters consists of five sets of triplets sisters and Oonga, the only single child. It's unclear if all of them come from the same family or different individual families. Massive Numbered Siblings: The Sixteen Swedish Sisters lives up to their name by actually having 16 sisters in the band. Same-Sex Triplets: The sisters consist of 5 sets of triplets, all of whom are female.

characters.name: Alaska Alan
characters.description: A very prominent Internet travel critic who Wolf and Honeybee try to impress in “Ghouls Rush in Adventure” Fun with Acronyms: Multiple times, Alaska Alan is just referred to as the abbreviation of Alaska followed by his first initial, AKA, often used in close proximity to the other AKA acronym, "also known as". Improperly Paranoid: He has PTSD from being kidnapped and tortured for a bad review he gave once before, thinks the Tobins and their guests are planning to do kill him over a series of coincidences and calls the police on them. It's not until they get back to the marina and they talk it over when Alan learns they actually were trying to tailor the tour to him to get a good review for their business from him.
